regions.name: Rioja
regions.location: Along the upper Ebro River in La Rioja, with parts of the Basque Country (Álava) and Navarra
regions.style: Red wines aged in oak and labeled by time in barrel and bottle: Crianza, Reserva, Gran Reserva.
facts: Spain's first DOCa (Denominación de Origen Calificada), awarded in 1991
Three subzones: Rioja Alta, Rioja Alavesa and Rioja Oriental
The Sierra de Cantabria shields the vineyards from Atlantic weather

regions.name: Navarra
regions.location: North-central Spain, from the Pyrenean foothills south to the Ebro River
regions.style: Fruit-forward reds and some of Spain's best-known dry rosés (rosados) made from Garnacha.
facts: Climate shifts from Atlantic in the north to Mediterranean in the south
Neighbors Rioja to the west and Aragón to the east
Rosado from Garnacha is the signature style

regions.name: Rías Baixas
regions.location: Galicia, on the Atlantic coast around the Galician inlets (rías)
regions.style: Crisp, aromatic, saline whites with high acidity. Albariño is the star.
facts: Cool, wet Atlantic climate with granite soils
Vines are often trained high on pergolas (parras) to fight humidity
Subzones include Val do Salnés, Condado do Tea and O Rosal

regions.name: Ribera del Duero
regions.location: A high-altitude stretch of the Duero River valley across Burgos, Segovia, Soria and Valladolid
regions.style: Powerful, structured, deeply colored reds, often oak aged.
facts: Vineyards sit roughly 750 to 900 meters above sea level
Big swings between hot days and cold nights keep acidity fresh
Tempranillo is locally called Tinto Fino or Tinta del País

regions.name: Rueda
regions.location: South of the Duero River around Valladolid, Segovia and Ávila
regions.style: Fresh, herbal, citrusy whites. Verdejo is the signature grape.
facts: Stony river-pebble soils and a continental climate
Harvesting at night is common to keep the grapes cool and fresh
Rueda Superior must contain at least 85% Verdejo

regions.name: Bierzo
regions.location: A mountain-ringed valley in León, in the northwest of Castilla y León
regions.style: Fragrant, mineral reds from Mencía and textured whites from Godello.
facts: Mountains around the valley let in some Atlantic influence
Slate and clay soils on steep hillsides
Mencía is the leading red grape

regions.name: Toro
regions.location: Along the Duero River in Zamora, west of Rueda
regions.style: Bold, tannic, high-alcohol reds with dark fruit.
facts: Tinta de Toro is the local clone of Tempranillo
Extreme continental climate with hot summers and cold winters
Many old vines on sandy soils

regions.name: Jumilla
regions.location: High plateau in Murcia, extending into Albacete
regions.style: Ripe, dark, full-bodied reds. Monastrell dominates.
facts: Hot, dry climate on a plateau about 400 to 800 meters up
Sandy, limestone soils helped many old vines survive
Monastrell is the same grape as France's Mourvèdre

regions.name: Alicante
regions.location: Mediterranean coast and inland valleys of Alicante province
regions.style: Warm-climate reds and aromatic Moscatel whites, plus the historic sweet Fondillón.
facts: Sea breezes moderate the Mediterranean heat
Garnacha Tintorera is also known as Alicante Bouschet
Fondillón is a historic sweet wine from this area

regions.name: Valencia
regions.location: Inland hills behind the Mediterranean coast of Valencia province
regions.style: Easy-drinking reds and whites, plus sweet Moscatel de Valencia.
facts: Subzones include Alto Turia, Valentino, Clariano and Moscatel de Valencia
Bobal is a major local red grape
Mediterranean climate with warm summers

regions.name: Getariako Txakolina
regions.location: Basque coast of Gipuzkoa, on the Bay of Biscay
regions.style: Very dry, high-acid, lightly spritzy white. Often poured from a height.
facts: Steep vineyards run right down to the Bay of Biscay
Hondarrabi Zuri is the main white grape
Traditionally poured from above the glass to add a little fizz

regions.name: Penedès
regions.style: Heart of Cava country, plus fresh still whites and reds.
facts: Cava, Spain's traditional-method sparkling wine, is centered here
Xarel·lo, Macabeo and Parellada are the classic Cava trio
Three zones: Alt, Mitjà and Baix Penedès, from hills down to the coast

regions.name: Priorat
regions.location: Mountains of Tarragona province in Catalonia
regions.style: Concentrated, mineral, powerful reds from low-yielding old vines.
facts: Vines grow on steep terraces of dark slate soil called llicorella
Qualified status (DOQ) is the Catalan name for DOCa
Garnacha and Cariñena lead the blends

regions.name: Montsant
regions.location: Wraps around Priorat in Tarragona province
regions.style: Rich red wines similar in grapes to Priorat, often at friendlier prices.
facts: Surrounds Priorat on three sides
Named for the Montsant mountain range
Granted its own DO in 2001

regions.name: Campo de Borja
regions.location: Zaragoza province in Aragón, near the Moncayo mountain
regions.style: Juicy, spicy Garnacha reds, often from old bush vines.
facts: Nicknamed the "Empire of Garnacha"
The cold, dry cierzo wind blows through the vineyards
Many old, low bush vines

regions.name: Canary Islands
regions.designation: Multiple DOs (e.g. Lanzarote, La Palma, Tacoronte-Acentejo)
regions.location: Atlantic islands off the coast of Morocco, far southwest of mainland Spain
regions.style: Volcanic, salty, mineral whites and light, spicy reds.
facts: Volcanic soils and Atlantic trade winds
Many ungrafted, very old vines
On Lanzarote, vines grow in pits (hoyos) shielded by stone walls

regions.name: Jerez (Sherry)
regions.location: Cádiz province, in the "Sherry Triangle" of Jerez, Sanlúcar de Barrameda and El Puerto de Santa María
regions.style: Fortified wines from bone-dry Fino to sweet Pedro Ximénez, aged in a solera system.
facts: Bright white albariza chalk soils hold water through the dry summer
Palomino is the main grape for dry sherries
Sanlúcar's coastal air helps make Manzanilla
regions.noWinesText: Sherries are covered in the Sherry section.
